records.description: Arevon develops, finances, builds, owns, and operates utility-scale solar generation and battery storage projects in the United States. Its customers are primarily utilities, community-choice aggregators, and other offtakers that procure power and capacity under long-term project contracts. The company follows an asset-heavy independent power producer model that combines development, construction, ownership, and long-term operation of contracted renewable assets. As of 2025 public disclosures described more than 5.3 gigawatts of operating solar and storage capacity across 17 states, roughly 1 gigawatt under construction, and more than $10 billion of operating assets. The platform was formed in 2021 from Capital Dynamics' U.S. clean energy infrastructure team and the Arevon asset-management business and has continued to scale through project financings and new project completions. Arevon was formed in August 2021 with backing from APG, CalSTRS, and a wholly owned subsidiary of ADIA, and current ownership percentages are not publicly disclosed.

records.description: FirstEnergy Transmission is the holding platform for FirstEnergy's regulated transmission businesses, including ATSI, MAIT, and TrAILCo. Its customers are transmission users served through regional grid tariffs, with revenues derived from regulated rate frameworks rather than merchant power sales. The business operates an asset-heavy utility model centered on long-lived transmission networks and related grid-investment programs across the Mid-Atlantic and Midwest. Public disclosures describe a system of roughly 24,000 transmission miles spanning multiple states within PJM and adjacent markets. Brookfield first acquired a 19.9% minority stake in 2022 and increased its position through a second transaction that closed in 2024, while FirstEnergy remained the operator and controlling owner. ADIA's exposure is publicly described as an indirect interest through Brookfield's infrastructure vehicle rather than as a separately disclosed direct stake in FET.

records.description: Sempra Infrastructure develops and operates LNG, energy networks, and lower-carbon infrastructure across North America. Its customer base includes utilities, LNG buyers, industrial counterparties, and other energy-market participants, and its operating model combines long-lived, asset-heavy infrastructure with a mix of contracted services and commodity-linked activity. The platform is headquartered in Houston and its principal assets and development projects are concentrated in Texas, Louisiana, and Mexico. Public disclosures describe the business as one of North America's larger private energy infrastructure platforms, anchored by LNG export, pipeline, storage, and related assets. Sempra completed the sale of a 30% non-controlling interest in Sempra Infrastructure to KKR and ADIA on June 1, 2022, leaving Sempra with a 70% controlling stake. In September 2025, Sempra announced an agreement that would change the ownership structure, but the company still described the 70%/20%/10% structure as current pending that future closing.

records.description: Alberta Schools Alternative Procurement I is a public-private partnership covering 18 school facilities in Calgary and Edmonton. The project serves provincial education authorities, school boards, students, and local communities through a long-term availability-based social infrastructure model. Public materials describe the scope as design, construction, finance, and lifecycle maintenance rather than direct education service provision. Amber-managed International Public Partnerships has identified the project within its education portfolio, and the schools were originally procured by the Province of Alberta under its school P3 program. Reviewed public sources do not disclose the current project-level ownership split within the investment vehicle.

records.description: Conterra Networks provides middle-mile and last-mile fiber and fixed wireless broadband services and designs, deploys, and operates customized networks, with a stated focus on underserved areas. Its customer base includes enterprise, carrier, education, government, and data-center users. The business is asset-heavy, owning and operating a fiber network that Fiera Infrastructure described at 11,600 route miles across 21 states and that the company later described at 15,000 miles across 22 states. Public materials place the operating footprint across the Southeast, South Central, and Western United States, with headquarters in Charlotte, North Carolina. Fiera Infrastructure first acquired an indirect equity interest in 2019 through EICLP and EISCSp, and APG joined Fiera in a later transaction that closed in 2021. Public disclosures also note significant participation by the senior management team, while current ownership percentages are not publicly disclosed.

records.description: IonicBlue is an energy-as-a-service provider that develops, finances, and manages building-efficiency and decarbonization projects for commercial, institutional, and public-sector customers. The business packages energy upgrades such as HVAC, controls, lighting, and related infrastructure into contracted service arrangements so customers can avoid large upfront capital expenditures. Its operating footprint spans the United States and Canada, and public materials describe the platform as a joint venture combining Johnson Controls' technical capabilities with Apollo's capital. Johnson Controls stated in 2023 that IonicBlue was founded in 2021 and had received up to C$100 million of additional capital from the Canada Infrastructure Bank to support Canadian projects. The platform was formed in 2021 through a joint venture between Johnson Controls and Apollo infrastructure funds, while public sources do not disclose the current ownership percentages.

records.description: US Wind develops offshore wind generation projects off the coast of Maryland. The platform serves utility and wholesale power markets through an asset-heavy development model focused on federal leasehold rights, permitting, interconnection, and long-term offtake arrangements. Public materials describe an 80,000-acre federal lease area and a development program capable of supporting roughly 1,500 MW to 1,800 MW of generation. The company has been active since 2011 and has advanced both state-level offtake awards and federal permitting milestones for its Maryland offshore projects. Apollo announced in 2020 that its infrastructure funds had made a strategic investment in US Wind, whose controlling shareholder is associated with Renexia, while public sources do not disclose the ownership percentages.

records.description: Lincoln Terminal Holdings provides rail transloading, storage, and logistics infrastructure for renewable fuels and related products. Its customers include fuel producers, distributors, and other supply-chain participants, and the business follows an asset-heavy terminaling model based on owned and operated infrastructure. records.description: MXT Holdings develops, owns, and operates neutral-host telecommunications infrastructure in Mexico, including towers and metropolitan fiber assets. Its customers are mobile network operators and other communications users that require shared infrastructure rather than single-tenant proprietary networks. The operating model is asset-heavy and lease driven, with recurring revenue tied to long-lived telecom sites and network infrastructure. The platform is focused on Mexico and is positioned around neutral-host infrastructure that supports carrier densification and connectivity demand. Ardian announced in 2023 that it had acquired a 50% co-control equity interest in MXT Holdings, which it described as its first direct investment in Mexico.

records.description: InTransit BC is the concessionaire responsible for the Canada Line rapid transit system in Metro Vancouver. The system serves urban commuters, airport passengers, and local transit users through a long-term public-private partnership with TransLink. Its operating model is asset-heavy and concession-based, with value tied to long-lived rail infrastructure and contractual payments rather than merchant transportation demand alone. Public sources describe the Canada Line as an 18-kilometre system with 16 stations linking downtown Vancouver, Richmond, and Vancouver International Airport. Operations are concentrated in British Columbia under a 35-year concession that runs to 2040. BCI's pooled-fund disclosures report a 28.7% interest in InTransit BC, while full public disclosure of the remaining ownership group is limited.
